title: A continuous linear map has a uniform norm bound
statement: Let $F$ be a field with a nontrivial real-valued absolute value $|\cdot|$ (there is $u\in F$ with $|u|\notin\{0,1\}$). Let $V,W$ be $F$-vector spaces with norms $N_V,N_W$: each norm is nonnegative, vanishes exactly at zero, satisfies the triangle inequality, and satisfies $N(cv)=|c|N(v)$ for $c\in F$. Give them the topologies from the distances $N_V(v-v')$ and $N_W(w-w')$. For every continuous $F$-linear map $f:V\to W$ there is a real constant $C>0$ such that $N_W(f(v))\le C N_V(v)$ for all $v\in V$. No completeness is assumed, and neither space is required to be finite-dimensional [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace].
